The difference between them is an observed outcome. It should not automatically be called a hidden PikoBuy fee because the payment channel, network, issuer and timing can contribute.

Compare against a timestamped reference without turning it into a promise

A public reference rate can be a benchmark, but match the currency pair, direction and date as closely as possible. Visa's official calculator describes its result as an indication of the rate a cardholder may receive. Mastercard's official converter says its result is indicative, that an issuer may use another rate or add fees, and that authorization or processing time can determine the applied rate. Those limitations are exactly why the settled statement remains primary evidence.

Calculate an observed comparison only after the transaction posts. Reference-value cost = checkout amount × reference rate. Observed difference = adjusted settled amount − reference-value cost. Observed difference percentage = observed difference ÷ reference-value cost × 100. Label the result as a transaction-specific difference, not an advertised markup.

Do not compare a weekend settlement with a rate captured days later, combine two different currency directions, or use a search-result snippet as the benchmark. Also avoid comparing a rate that excludes fees with a settled total that includes them. A clean comparison tells you what happened; it does not prove who caused every basis point.

Handle pending transactions, partial refunds and account balance separately

A pending authorization is provisional. It may change, disappear or be replaced when the transaction posts. Do not finalize an observed rate from the hold. Record both values if they differ and mark settlement as the closing checkpoint.

For a full or partial refund, preserve the original payment. Add the refunded source amount, returned home-currency amount, refund date and any explicit deduction. Calculate a separate observed refund rate only when you can match the returned amount to a defined source-currency refund. Subtracting the refund from the purchase and calculating one blended rate hides timing and deduction effects.

Account balance introduces another boundary. If a refund lands in platform balance rather than the original payment account, it has not yet become a home-currency cash return. Record the credited amount and currency, then treat any later balance use or withdrawal as a separate event. PikoBuy's public shipping terms also mention account-balance deductions for cash-on-delivery forwarding fees; do not merge such a deduction with an unrelated card conversion.

Worked example: reconcile one payment with neutral values

Suppose a checkout shows 1,000 units in its transaction currency. The final bank record posts 137.50 units in the home currency, including a separately labelled 2.50-unit foreign-transaction fee. These are illustrative units, not a live PikoBuy quote or current market rate.

  1. Remove the explicit 2.50 fee from 137.50, leaving 135.00 for the rate calculation.
  2. Calculate 135.00 ÷ 1,000 = 0.135 home-currency units per checkout unit.
  3. Record 2.50 separately as an issuer-side fee shown on the statement.
  4. If a timestamp-matched reference rate is 0.132, calculate a benchmark value of 132.00.
  5. The observed rate difference is 135.00 − 132.00 = 3.00 home-currency units.
  6. The observed difference percentage is 3.00 ÷ 132.00 × 100, or about 2.27%.

The conclusion is limited: this transaction settled 3.00 units above that benchmark before the explicit issuer fee. The evidence does not by itself assign the difference to PikoBuy, a wallet, a card network, a bank or timing. Repeat the method across several settled transactions before treating the result as a planning range.

Build a currency worksheet that remains auditable

Use one row per payment event. Suggested columns are order or parcel category, event date, source amount and currency, checkout amount and currency, labelled platform lines, authorization amount, settled amount and currency, explicit payment-side fee, adjusted settled amount, observed rate direction, reference source and timestamp, observed difference, refund link and notes.

Add an evidence status: checkout captured, pending only, settled, adjusted or unresolved. A row should not enter averages until it is settled and reconciled. For comparisons, group transactions by the same currency pair and payment method; otherwise, the average can disguise different conversion paths.

Plan future costs with a range rather than copying one observed rate forever. Use a low, central and high planning assumption, label the date, and refresh it before payment. Keep the product, domestic delivery, platform service line, international shipping and destination costs outside the currency-difference row unless your calculation explicitly defines their inclusion.

Escalate when the currency code is missing, the checkout and authorization cannot be matched, an explicit fee is unexplained, the settled amount changes after posting, or a refund lacks a traceable relationship to the original payment. The goal is a reproducible record, not a forced explanation.
intro: A reference rate is not a receipt. Measure conversion from the checkout, authorization and settled transaction that belong together, then keep explicit fees and timing differences visible.

title: Why Does PikoBuy Charge Shipping Twice?
description: Understand why PikoBuy can show two shipping charges: seller-to-warehouse delivery first, then a separate international parcel payment.
body:
PikoBuy domestic shipping ends at warehouse receipt

For a purchasing order, the domestic leg begins when the seller dispatches the selected item inside China and ends when the PikoBuy warehouse receives it. The product price buys the item. Seller-to-warehouse delivery moves it to storage. International shipping begins only after approved warehouse items are packed into a parcel, a route is chosen and that parcel charge is paid.

PikoBuy’s current beginner guide presents these events as separate stages: choose specifications, colour and size; submit and pay the purchasing order; wait for warehouse inspection; then choose a shipping route and pay international shipping. That sequence is the reason a domestic delivery line should never be merged into a later freight estimate merely because both contain the word “shipping.”

Use one definition throughout your records. “Domestic” means seller or sender to warehouse. “International” means warehouse parcel to destination. A warehouse return to the seller is another domestic movement, but it belongs to an after-sales scenario rather than the original inbound line.

Follow evidence from the source page to the warehouse event

The earliest domestic amount may appear on the selected source listing or purchasing-order summary. Treat it as current evidence, not a permanent platform rate. The amount can depend on the seller, delivery terms, address, quantity or how the seller groups products. Save the selected product state and the order record together so you know what the charge relates to.

Then follow four checkpoints: order submitted, seller dispatch recorded, domestic tracking or handoff evidence available, and warehouse receipt. PikoBuy’s guide says the warehouse performs check-in, photo confirmation and a defect check after arrival. The warehouse event therefore confirms that something reached the facility; it does not automatically prove that every item, option or charge in a multi-item order was correct.

CheckpointEvidence to keepQuestion answered
Source selectionSeller, exact variant, quantity and delivery contextWhat did the order intend to acquire?
Paid orderProduct and domestic lines as recordedWhat was accepted at payment?
Seller dispatchStatus, grouping and any available domestic referenceWhich seller shipment is moving?
Warehouse receiptArrival time, item identity and inspection recordWhat actually reached the warehouse?

Give every seller-to-warehouse charge its own ledger row

Create a domestic-shipping ledger before the items arrive. Use columns for order ID, seller, item IDs, source platform, quantity, recorded domestic amount, evidence location, status and last checked date. Keep the original currency. If you need a planning currency, store the conversion and date in separate columns so a currency movement is not mistaken for a delivery change.

Domestic acquisition subtotal = selected product amounts + confirmed inbound domestic charges + approved order adjustments

This subtotal stops at the warehouse. Do not add packaging, international route estimates, destination taxes or return costs. Label each domestic row as confirmed , provisional , included , cash on delivery , or unresolved only when the current evidence supports that label. A blank amount is unknown; it is not automatically free.

Record adjustments as new rows. If the purchasing record changes after the seller confirms availability or scope, do not overwrite the original amount without explanation. A dated adjustment makes the final reconciliation understandable and prevents an order-stage difference from being blamed on international freight.

Reconcile seller groups before allocating cost to individual items

One seller shipment may contain several items, while several sellers normally create separate domestic movements. Start by matching the charge to the seller shipment, not by dividing every amount across every product in the account. A group-level charge should remain attached to that group until you need a per-item analysis.

For internal budgeting, choose and document an allocation rule. Equal division is simple when units are similar. Quantity share can work when identical units travel together. Product-value share may be useful for an acquisition-cost comparison, but it does not claim the seller calculated shipping that way. Keep both the original group charge and the editorial allocation so the platform record remains intact.

Do not double count. If two item rows point to one seller charge, mark the line once at group level and let the item rows reference it. If one seller dispatch is split into two domestic packages, keep two tracking or receipt events but verify whether the paid domestic charge changed before adding a second cost line.

Forwarded goods need a sender-to-warehouse record

PikoBuy’s current Shipping Terms describe a forwarding workflow that is distinct from a normal purchasing order: obtain the warehouse address, give it to the sender, submit the forwarding form, wait for receipt and photos, then submit the goods as a parcel. In this case, your domestic ledger starts with the sender and the forwarding form rather than a PikoBuy purchasing order.

The same terms say that if a forwarded parcel arrives with shipping fee payable on delivery, PikoBuy can deduct that amount from the account balance without separate confirmation. This is a specific cash-on-delivery forwarding condition; do not generalize it to every marketplace order. Record the sender’s reference, forwarding form, expected package count and account deduction evidence.

The terms also tell users to contact the sender if goods are missing on warehouse receipt and state that PikoBuy does not provide after-sales service for forwarded products, although it can help ship goods back. That makes sender identity and packing evidence especially important for this workflow.

Worked example: two sellers, three items and one grouped charge

Assume Item A and Item B come from Seller One, while Item C comes from Seller Two. The paid order shows one inbound domestic line for A and B together and a separate line for C. Do not copy Seller One’s group amount into both item rows; that would count the same charge twice.

  1. Create Group S1 containing A and B, with its single domestic line and order evidence.
  2. Create Group S2 containing C, with its separate domestic line.
  3. Keep both charges in the original currency and mark whether each is confirmed or provisional.
  4. When Seller One dispatches two packages, add two receipt checkpoints under Group S1 without inventing a second charge.
  5. When A arrives first, mark A received and B in transit; do not mark the whole group complete.
  6. After B arrives, reconcile the group’s package count, item identity and recorded domestic amount.
  7. If a per-item budget is needed, allocate the S1 amount once using a documented rule while retaining the original group total.

The calculation is structural: total inbound domestic cost equals the confirmed S1 group line plus the confirmed S2 line. The example intentionally uses no fabricated currency amount or fixed PikoBuy tariff. Your live order records supply the values.

Close the domestic ledger only after warehouse review

Arrival is the right moment to compare expected seller, item, variant, quantity and package group with the warehouse record. If one item is missing, avoid assuming the warehouse lost it. Check whether the seller split the dispatch, whether another package is still moving and whether the order scope changed. For forwarded goods, the published terms specifically direct missing-item verification to the sender.

If the received item has a seller-caused problem, keep the original inbound charge and any potential return movement separate. PikoBuy’s current Returns & Exchanges page says responsibility and costs depend on the reason, seller agreement, item condition and eligibility. For eligible customer-choice returns, the published terms can include the seller’s original shipping and shipping back to the seller; seller-caused cases are handled differently. Verify the live case rather than forecasting a universal deduction.

Close a row when the correct item has been received, its domestic amount is reconciled, and no unresolved package remains. The next cost stage is warehouse and parcel planning—not a continuation of the seller’s domestic line.
intro: Domestic delivery is the China leg between the seller and the warehouse. It deserves its own evidence trail because it can change before receipt, appear once for a group of items, or be confused with the international parcel charge paid later.

title: PikoBuy Parcel Reinforcement: Cost vs Damage Risk
description: Compare PikoBuy parcel reinforcement cost with crush, impact and movement risk using current packing options, final dimensions and an evidence-based decision model.
body:
PikoBuy confirms reinforcement requests, not one universal package

PikoBuy's current beginner guide says that after warehouse check-in, photo confirmation and defect checking, users can add requests such as minimal packaging or reinforced packaging. That confirms a choice exists in the public workflow. It does not define one permanent material list, price, weight increase, dimension change or damage guarantee.

The public guide also says users choose a shipping route and that routes differ in delivery time and billing methods. PikoBuy's shipping terms say parcels are carried by third-party logistics providers and that logistics risks such as damage and loss cannot be eliminated. Reinforcement should therefore be treated as one risk-control input, not a promise that a parcel will arrive unharmed.

Before selecting anything, capture the live option name, description, current charge, parcel items, packaging state and check date. If the interface does not say what the option changes, ask through the current support channel. Do not assume that the word “reinforced” always means corner guards, a stronger box, wrapping, extra tape or double boxing.

Name the failure mode before paying for extra protection

“Damage risk” is too broad for a useful decision. Separate four failure modes. Crush affects structures that deform under stacking. Impact threatens brittle items and edges. Movement allows products to collide or rub. Puncture or abrasion threatens soft packaging near hard corners.

Moisture, leakage, temperature and dangerous-goods compliance are different problems. A stronger carton may do little for an unsealed liquid. Confirm that the service addresses the identified failure instead of treating every add-on as interchangeable.

Use warehouse evidence to map vulnerability: fragile materials, hollow shapes, collectible boxes, sharp hardware, rigid corners, heavy objects beside light ones and empty space. PikoBuy says professional inspection is unavailable for every special product, so photos do not establish hidden strength or transit durability.

Turn a vague reinforcement request into a measurable objective

Write one sentence describing the goal: prevent carton collapse around a rigid box, keep two hard items from striking each other, protect exposed corners, or reduce movement around a delicate product. The objective should point to a packing change that can be confirmed after the parcel is prepared.

Carrier packaging guidance illustrates why objectives differ. Common methods include using a strong outer container, filling empty spaces to limit movement, cushioning items individually and using a second outer box for certain fragile or sharp goods. These are general transport principles, not statements about which PikoBuy service is currently included. The live PikoBuy description remains the authority for the option you are buying.

Avoid requesting maximum material without considering trade-offs. Extra layers can add mass and expand external dimensions. A larger carton can raise volumetric or billable weight, cross a route threshold or remove an otherwise eligible method. Too much rigid packing can also be unnecessary for soft, durable goods. The goal is suitable protection for the actual contents, not the largest possible parcel.

Compare total decision cost, not just the reinforcement line

The direct reinforcement charge is only one field. Record the current service amount and currency, then estimate how the packing change could affect international shipping. Keep unknown values labelled rather than filling them with figures from another platform or an old screenshot.

Cost fieldEvidence to recordDecision question
Direct add-onLive option and checkout amountWhat service is the charge for?
Added weightFinal packed scale recordDid materials change the weight step?
Added volumeFinal outer dimensionsDid protection enlarge billable volume?
Route changeEligible methods before and afterWas a route lost or gained?
Damage exposureContents and failure-mode notesWhat loss is the option intended to reduce?
ConcentrationValue and vulnerability in one parcelWould splitting isolate incompatible items?

Do not claim a precise probability of damage without relevant shipment data. Use decision bands instead: low concern when contents are soft and mutually compatible; medium concern when retail packaging or hard hardware matters; high concern when brittle, irregular or heavy items can damage themselves or neighbours. The band guides investigation—it is not an insurance rating.

Recalculate weight, dimensions and route eligibility after packing

Reinforcement can change the same fields used by PikoBuy's public estimator: weight, length, width and height. A larger outer box can materially increase occupied volume.

Use the final packed state. Save actual weight, outer dimensions, product type, destination, route, displayed billable weight and current rounding method. Never combine pre-reinforcement dimensions with post-reinforcement scale weight.

Compare before and after as separate scenarios. Keep the shipping difference distinct from the add-on price, platform fees and currency conversion. A cheap-looking option can have a larger indirect cost if it creates another billing step.

Decision cost = current add-on charge + observed change in parcel shipping cost

This is a worksheet structure, not a guaranteed formula; only the current checkout shows the payable amount.

Worked comparison: three parcels need different answers

Consider three hypothetical warehouse groups. The examples contain no PikoBuy price, damage rate or service promise.

Parcel A: soft clothing only

Three folded garments have no rigid presentation boxes, sharp parts or fragile decorations. The main concern is moisture or surface contamination, not crushing. Generic outer reinforcement may have limited value unless the live service addresses a known weakness. Record the available packing choices and avoid adding volume without a clear objective.

Parcel B: collectible box inside a mixed parcel

A display box matters to the buyer and sits beside dense accessories. Crushing, corner impact and internal movement are plausible failure modes. Ask what reinforcement protects, whether items are separated and how final dimensions will change. The buyer may accept a higher total cost because the retail box itself carries value, but that choice should be explicit.

Parcel C: brittle irregular object

A fragile, irregular object has exposed edges and limited visible evidence about internal strength. PikoBuy's terms warn that items such as ceramics, glass and irregular shapes can be damaged during repeated transport. First confirm route eligibility and whether the available packing method addresses impact and movement. If the risk remains unacceptable, reinforcement alone should not turn the parcel into an automatic ship decision.

  1. List every item and its vulnerable feature.
  2. Name the dominant failure mode.
  3. Read the live reinforcement description and price.
  4. Confirm whether the option changes separation, cushioning or outer strength.
  5. Save the predicted weight and dimension effect as an estimate.
  6. Compare alternative grouping or removal decisions.
  7. Select only after checking eligible routes.
  8. Reconcile the final packed parcel before payment.

Verify the result after the parcel is reinforced

A request is not the same as evidence that the requested outcome was achieved. When a post-packing image or measurement is available, confirm the parcel state without expecting photos to prove hidden cushioning. Check visible box condition, sealed edges, exposed protrusions, item separation where observable, and whether the recorded dimensions describe the same final parcel.

Save the service label, charge, request time, completed packing state, final weight, final dimensions and selected route in one record. If a critical objective cannot be confirmed, ask before authorizing shipment. Do not overwrite the earlier scenario; the before-and-after comparison explains the cost change.

Reinforcement also does not replace route restrictions, accurate declarations, insurance review or careful delivery inspection. PikoBuy's terms place some fragile-item and third-party logistics risks on the user and distinguish insurance from packing. Preserve evidence of the outer parcel at receipt when damage is visible, and follow the current support and claim rules rather than assuming the packing add-on guarantees compensation.
intro: Reinforcement is useful only when it answers a specific failure risk. Name what could be damaged, verify the current packing option and charge, then recalculate the finished parcel instead of buying “more protection” by instinct.

title: PikoBuy Restricted Goods and Route Availability: Screen a Parcel Before Shipping
description: Screen PikoBuy restricted goods through platform, carrier, route and destination gates before paying for an international parcel.
body:
Restricted-goods screening starts with item identity

“Clothing,” “electronics” and “cosmetics” are too broad for a shipping decision. Record the product name, source page, exact selected variant, quantity, material or ingredient description, included accessories, power source, liquid or powder content, magnet or pressurised component, package state and date checked. The route question applies to that complete item, not its marketing category.

Open the current product and order records rather than relying on a spreadsheet title. A jacket may include a removable battery. A toy may contain magnets. A grooming set may include liquid. A shoe-care kit may contain adhesive. Those components can change the screening result even when the main product appears ordinary.

Separate known, seller-stated and unknown fields. A seller description is evidence of what was claimed, not independent proof of composition or safe transport classification. If an ingredient, battery specification or included part is unclear, write the uncertainty down and ask a precise question. Do not edit the description to make a route appear.

Use four gates instead of one “restricted” label

A useful screening process distinguishes four decisions:

  1. Platform gate: whether PikoBuy's current rules permit the item to be purchased, forwarded, stored or handled.
  2. Carrier and route gate: whether a live shipping option accepts the declared contents, package and destination.
  3. Export and transit gate: whether the shipment complies with rules that apply where it leaves and passes through.
  4. Destination gate: whether the recipient country permits import and any separate product requirements can be met.

Passing an earlier gate does not prove the next one. Warehouse acceptance is not international-carrier acceptance. A route displayed for one ordinary parcel is not evidence that it accepts a battery, liquid or fragile item. Carrier acceptance does not override customs law, and customs release does not establish that a regulated product may lawfully be sold or used.

Record pass, fail or confirmation needed at each gate. Add the rule source, date, exact product scope and the person or interface that supplied the answer. One undifferentiated “sensitive” tag hides the reason and makes a later recheck almost impossible.

Read PikoBuy's current rules as boundaries, not a complete route list

PikoBuy's service agreement says users are responsible for understanding internationally prohibited items and relevant laws. Its prohibited-mailing section includes goods barred by law, dangerous items such as explosive, flammable, corrosive, radioactive or toxic materials, currency, items that may endanger public health, perishables and other items unsuitable for mailing. Treat that published list as a hard warning, not an invitation to find a more permissive route.

The same agreement identifies examples of sensitive or higher-risk contents, including essential oils, care solutions, lubricants, batteries and glue. It also flags replicas and items containing large amounts of liquid or powder, batteries, food or medicine as customs-risk categories. These examples are not a complete catalogue of every restricted item, country or carrier rule.

PikoBuy also says sensitive contents may be removed during handling, and that professional inspection may not be possible for some specialised products. If removal would change the product, value or safety of the order, resolve that possibility before authorising purchase or parcel submission. Do not assume an ordinary warehouse photo can determine a technical dangerous-goods classification.

Verify route availability with the finished parcel

PikoBuy's current shipping estimator asks for destination, product type, weight, length, width and height. Its beginner guide says routes differ in delivery time and billing methods. For restricted-goods screening, the product attributes are equally important: use the live parcel workflow after the contents and packaging are final, not a cached result from an empty or different parcel.

Create a parcel manifest with one row per item and component. Include quantity, declared attribute, supporting evidence, whether original packaging remains, and any warehouse note. Then compare the manifest with the route's current acceptance wording. Record the route name, quote time and eligibility result exactly as displayed.

If no route appears, do not repeatedly change the category or omit a component. First confirm that destination, weight and dimensions are valid; then ask which declared content prevents eligibility. A route appearing after a different description is not permission to misdescribe the parcel.

If a route appears, inspect its content limits, packaging conditions and any confirmation notice. A displayed quote is evidence of a current interface result for the declared inputs. It is not proof that undeclared contents are accepted or that customs will release the parcel.

Check destination law and product rules separately

The receiving country can prohibit or condition import even when the platform and carrier accept the shipment. Search the destination customs, postal, transport-safety and relevant product regulator sources for the exact item. Use the current commodity description, components, quantity and intended use. General shopping advice and another buyer's successful parcel are not legal evidence.

Distinguish a prohibition from a permit, licence, quantity threshold, labelling rule, tax rule or product-safety requirement. Each creates a different action. “Allowed with documentation” is not the same as unrestricted, and payment of tax does not legalise an otherwise prohibited import.

PikoBuy's agreement explicitly says it makes no guarantee regarding customs clearance and notes that authorities may request invoices or other clearance documents. Keep truthful commercial descriptions, purchase records and any required supporting documents available. Never lower or alter a declaration to bypass a restriction.

Build an evidence record that survives a route change

Use a compact checklist for every potentially restricted item:

  • Product identifier, source URL, exact variant and quantity.
  • Complete components, battery or power details, liquids, powders, magnets, aerosols, adhesives and other relevant attributes.
  • Seller-stated specifications, label photos and unresolved questions.
  • PikoBuy handling status and the current rule or notice checked.
  • Final parcel ID, manifest revision, weight, dimensions and packaging.
  • Live route eligibility, restriction wording and quote timestamp.
  • Destination and transit source, check date and document requirement.
  • Decision owner, next action and recheck trigger.

Keep screenshots or exported records where permitted, but also transcribe the decisive text. Name the item and route in every note. “Support said okay” is weak evidence without the question, date and scope. “Confirmed for one sealed 10 ml item on Route X to Country Y, subject to the displayed conditions” is easier to audit.

Do not let this record become stale. Recheck before purchase when the item itself may be unacceptable, after warehouse inspection when attributes are confirmed, after packing when the route scenario is complete, and immediately before payment.

Three cases that show why the gates matter

Ordinary pullover with no declared sensitive component

The source describes a textile pullover and the warehouse evidence matches the selected variant. Record material claims and packaging, then run the live parcel. If eligible routes appear, continue to destination rules and normal comparison. “Ordinary” still does not create a customs guarantee.

Small electronic item with an included battery

The battery is part of the item identity, not an optional note. Save its stated type and specification, mark unknowns, and confirm platform handling. Check only routes that explicitly accept the declared battery scenario and destination. If the battery could be removed, create separate keep and remove scenarios; do not assume removal is safe or authorised.

Care product described as a liquid

Record volume, ingredients or safety information when available, container state and quantity. PikoBuy's terms identify care solutions and liquids as sensitive or customs-risk examples. Ask about the exact product and live route. If a lawful, clearly eligible route cannot be verified, reject or return the item rather than relabelling it as an ordinary accessory.

These cases do not predict acceptance. They show how complete identity produces a defensible question and prevents one successful route result from being copied across unlike products.

Make the shipping decision before money and risk are committed

Mark an item clear for current parcel review only when its identity is complete, the platform gate is satisfied, a live route accepts the declared scenario and destination requirements are understood. Mark it confirmation needed when one authoritative answer or document could resolve the issue. Mark it do not ship when a prohibition applies, truthful classification produces no eligible route, or required evidence cannot be obtained.

Before paying, compare the final parcel manifest with the route result line by line. Confirm that no item, battery, liquid, powder, accessory or packaging change was omitted. Save the current restriction terms, amount and timestamp. If the route disappears or its wording changes, stop and rebuild the decision from the updated evidence.

This process will sometimes end with no usable route. That is a valid result. The purpose of a PikoBuy restricted-goods check is not to force every purchase into a parcel; it is to identify when the safest and most lawful decision is to return, remove or avoid an item.
intro: Check route eligibility before buying and again before parcel payment. A product being available to purchase does not mean an international route accepts it for your destination.

title: PikoBuy Service and Payment Fees: Audit Every Charge Before Paying
description: Audit PikoBuy service and payment fees before paying: separate product, domestic delivery, shipping service fee, currency conversion and bank-side charges.
body:
PikoBuy service and payment fees are not one number

Start by separating four actors. The seller sets the product price and may create seller-to-warehouse delivery. PikoBuy records the purchasing and parcel workflows and may add the service lines described in its current terms. A third-party logistics provider supplies the international route. A payment network, wallet, bank or card issuer may convert currency or add a charge under its own agreement.

If all four are called “the PikoBuy fee,” you cannot explain why a total changed. Give every line a precise label: product, domestic delivery, purchase-stage service line, international shipping, shipping-stage platform service fee, payment-channel charge, issuer charge, currency conversion difference, return cost or destination-side amount.

The audit question is not “Is there a fee?” It is: who created the line, what amount is it based on, when is it shown, what currency does it use, and where can it be verified? A blank answer means unresolved—not zero.

What PikoBuy currently publishes about service charges

PikoBuy's current Terms of Service distinguish purchasing-agent and parcel-forwarding stages. They say third-party purchasers currently provide purchasing-agent services free of charge, while the user still prepays the chosen product cost and domestic logistics. The same section says PikoBuy may add a necessary service fee when the user confirms payment for purchased goods, but it does not publish a fixed purchase-stage percentage in that clause. Verify the exact live order summary rather than inventing a rate.

For cross-border parcel forwarding, the terms say the user pays the logistics provider's shipping fee and a platform service fee to PikoBuy. The published calculation is 8% of the shipping fee, with a warning that the actual calculation may differ slightly because of exchange-rate fluctuation and settlement timing. That is a current policy statement, not permission to assume every screen, currency or future checkout will remain unchanged.

PikoBuy's public footer currently displays card marks including Visa, Mastercard, American Express and JCB. A displayed mark indicates a payment-method family, not a promise that every card, country, currency or transaction will be accepted, and not proof that the method carries no separate charge. Confirm the methods and amounts shown for your account at payment time.

Audit the purchasing-order payment before authorization

At the first payment, begin with the exact selected product state. Confirm seller, colour, size, version, quantity and the price shown for that combination. PikoBuy's beginner guide says prices are subject to actual purchase and out-of-stock orders are refunded. Therefore, the selected source price, the purchasing-order total and any later adjustment should remain separate evidence points.

LineVerify thisDo not assume
ProductSelected variant, quantity and current amountCover or starting price applies
Domestic deliverySeller-to-warehouse amount and groupingBlank means free
Service lineLabel, base, amount and checkout currencyA fixed rate not shown live
DiscountEligibility, applied amount and expiryA banner guarantees checkout credit
Payment totalFinal amount submitted to the channelIt equals the bank's posted amount

Take a private record of the summary immediately before authorization. Do not publish card numbers, billing addresses, order IDs or account balances. If a line is unclear, pause and ask support what the label covers. A small unexplained amount should not be buried inside the product price merely to make the worksheet balance.

Audit the international parcel and its service-fee base

Parcel payment is a later event. PikoBuy's guide says the shopper chooses a suitable shipping route, submits the parcel and pays international shipping. The terms then identify the shipping fee and the platform service fee as separate obligations. Record the final route, packed weight and dimensions, shipping charge, service-fee line and checkout currency together.

Published shipping-stage platform service fee = international shipping fee × 8%

Use the shipping amount actually shown as the base. Do not apply 8% to the product price, domestic delivery, a previous route estimate or the entire landed-cost worksheet. If the checkout shows a converted amount or a small difference from your arithmetic, retain the displayed values and note the terms' exchange-rate and settlement-time qualification.

Optional packaging, insurance or other add-ons belong on their own rows only when the current parcel screen confirms them. The 8% formula does not prove that every additional service is included in or excluded from the base; the live labelled summary resolves that question. Route discounts should also remain visible instead of being netted silently against an unrelated line.

Separate platform calculation from currency and bank effects

Record three currency checkpoints: the currency used for the PikoBuy checkout, the currency authorized by the payment channel, and the currency posted by the bank or wallet. If they differ, save the amount at each stage and the timestamp. A change can result from conversion timing, payment-channel processing or issuer rules without being a new PikoBuy service fee.

Calculate an observed rate only from amounts that belong to the same transaction. Divide the posted home-currency amount by the authorized checkout-currency amount. Label the result “observed transaction rate,” not PikoBuy's permanent exchange rate. If a separate issuer fee appears, keep it outside the rate calculation so the two effects remain measurable.

Do not use a public mid-market quote as the expected card settlement total without checking the payment network and issuer terms. Likewise, do not infer a hidden percentage from one transaction when timing, refunds or pending authorizations may still change the record.

Worked example: test the published shipping service-fee formula

Assume a parcel checkout shows an international shipping fee of 500 units in the checkout currency. Under the current published 8% formula, the calculated platform service fee is 40 units, producing 540 units before any separately labelled option or payment-side effect.

  1. Save the route and final parcel inputs that produced the 500-unit shipping line.
  2. Calculate 500 × 0.08 = 40 as the expected service-fee line.
  3. Compare 40 with the value actually shown; do not replace the checkout value with your calculation.
  4. Check for separately labelled packing, insurance, discount or account-balance lines.
  5. Record the total submitted to the payment channel.
  6. After settlement, record the bank or wallet's posted amount and currency.
  7. Explain any difference with evidence instead of assigning it automatically to PikoBuy.

The example uses neutral units to demonstrate the calculation, not a live freight quote. It does not claim a route price, exchange rate, payment fee or card acceptance result. Your parcel screen and posted transaction supply those values.

Close the fee record only after payment settles

A pending authorization can change, disappear or be replaced by a settled transaction. Keep the pre-payment summary, authorized amount and posted amount as separate checkpoints. If a refund occurs, add the refund date, original-currency amount, returned amount and any explicitly labelled deduction. Do not erase the original payment.

PikoBuy's Returns & Exchanges page publishes separate return conditions and costs for eligible warehouse cases, including a current RMB 5 service fee for an unconditional return plus relevant domestic shipping lines. That rule belongs in a return record, not in the normal purchase or parcel service-fee calculation. Eligibility, responsibility and seller consent still need live verification.

A complete audit ends with three conclusions: the platform lines reconciled to the checkout; any currency or payment-side difference reconciled to the settled statement; and every unresolved line has an owner and next evidence point. This creates a reusable cost history without turning one order into a universal fee table.
intro: “Fee” can describe several different costs created by different parties. A reliable audit names the actor, calculation base, currency and evidence for each line before you authorize the order or parcel payment.

title: PikoBuy Shipping Line Comparison: Choose With Parcel Evidence
description: Compare PikoBuy shipping lines using live eligibility, billable weight, dimensions, tracking, cost and risk evidence for one finished parcel.
body:
Compare routes against one frozen parcel scenario

A route comparison becomes unreliable when each option uses a different destination, item group or measurement. Start with one scenario: destination country and region, complete item list, declared product attributes, final packaging choice, actual weight, outer length, width and height, and the date and time of the quote.

PikoBuy's public shipping estimator asks for destination, product type, weight and dimensions. Its beginner guide says users choose a suitable route when submitting a parcel and warns that routes differ in delivery time and billing methods. Those facts make the comparison parcel-specific. A screenshot or recommendation for another shipment is not a substitute for a fresh result.

Give the scenario a revision number. If you remove packaging, add reinforcement, split the contents or correct an item attribute, create a new revision and request new results. Do not compare Route A from the old parcel with Route B from the revised one.

The comparison date matters too. A route can change price, eligibility or terms after a saved spreadsheet was created. Treat every quote as a dated observation, not a promise that the same choice will exist later.

Eliminate ineligible routes before comparing price

Start with hard gates. Confirm that the destination, product attributes, parcel weight and dimensions fall within the current route rules. Check whether the contents include liquids, powders, batteries, magnets, fragile shapes, sharp parts, restricted goods or other declared attributes that affect acceptance.

PikoBuy's terms place responsibility on users to understand prohibited items and relevant laws. They also describe special risks for items such as liquids, powders, batteries, food, medicine, replicas, ceramics, glass and irregular shapes. These are risk signals, not a complete destination-specific acceptance list. The live route result and current destination rules still control the decision.

Record the eligibility result as eligible, ineligible or needs confirmation, followed by the exact reason shown. Never hide a restriction behind a high score. A cheap route that does not accept the parcel is not a candidate.

Separate platform screening, carrier acceptance, customs law and product compliance. Passing one layer does not guarantee passage through the next. When the wording is unclear, ask about the actual item and route rather than relabelling it to obtain a quote.

Normalize the current cost without erasing billing differences

Copy the displayed route name, currency, shipping amount, billable weight, weight step, billing basis and any visible service charge into the same row. Preserve actual weight and volumetric inputs beside the result. If a number is not shown, write “not shown” instead of borrowing a rate from an old article or another platform.

Routes can apply different billing methods. Compare the full current amount for the same parcel revision, not only a per-kilogram headline. Note rounding, minimum charge, dimensional treatment and included or optional services when the live terms state them.

FieldWhat to saveWhy it matters
ScenarioDestination, items, packaging revisionKeeps every quote comparable
Physical dataActual weight and outer dimensionsExplains the billed result
EligibilityPass, fail or confirmation neededRemoves unusable options
Current amountCurrency, route amount and visible feesShows the payable comparison
Billing evidenceBillable weight, step and stated methodPrevents false per-kilo comparisons
Quote timeDate and time capturedMarks the result as temporary

Keep destination taxes and charges outside the route quote unless the current terms explicitly include them. A route label should not be treated as a universal customs or tax promise.

Compare service evidence, not adjectives

Speed labels such as economy, standard or express are not comparable evidence by themselves. Record the current time range only when PikoBuy shows it for the exact route, destination and parcel, and preserve whether it is described as an estimate or guarantee. Do not publish one historical delivery as the route's normal time.

Then examine traceability. Save what the current terms say about tracking availability, carrier handoffs, proof of delivery and the point at which an inquiry may be opened. A route with fewer scans is not automatically lost, but lower visibility may be important for a time-sensitive or high-value parcel.

Identify the last-mile arrangement only when it is shown. International parcels may pass among several providers. A familiar route name does not prove which local carrier will deliver every parcel.

Add operational fit: deadline flexibility, tolerance for sparse tracking, value concentration, replacement difficulty and address constraints. These buyer-specific fields should influence the shortlist without being disguised as universal route quality.

Read risk, insurance and claim terms separately

PikoBuy's shipping terms state that parcels are carried by third-party logistics providers and list risks including customs action, damage, loss and peak-season delay. The service agreement says the user chooses the third-party provider and that compensation standards are subject to that provider. A route comparison should therefore preserve the applicable terms rather than promising an outcome.

If insurance is available, record the exact parcel eligibility, current price, insured amount, covered events, exclusions, evidence requirements and claim limit before paying. Do not treat the word “insurance” as identical coverage across routes. Packing and reinforcement are also separate controls; stronger packaging does not create insurance, and insurance does not prevent damage.

Use a simple exposure note: what can go wrong, what evidence would exist, what loss remains with the buyer and what condition would make the route unacceptable. Avoid invented probabilities. The goal is to reveal an unmanageable exposure, not calculate a fake precision score.

Build the shortlist with gates, then preferences

Apply the decision in two passes. In pass one, eliminate any route that fails destination, contents, weight, dimensions or a non-negotiable delivery requirement. Put unclear routes in a confirmation queue. In pass two, compare the remaining candidates on current total amount, billing method, stated time range, tracking evidence, claim terms and buyer preference.

Use a reasoned rank rather than a single weighted score. A score can conceal a critical weakness—for example, a low price offsetting unacceptable insurance terms. Write one sentence for each candidate: “kept because,” “held because” or “rejected because.”

A good shortlist may contain two choices. One can be the lower-cost option for a replaceable parcel with a flexible deadline; another can offer stronger traceability or terms for a harder-to-replace shipment. The choice is tied to the frozen scenario, not awarded permanently to a route name.

Worked case: three live candidates, no universal winner

Consider a finished parcel containing ordinary clothing and one rigid accessory. The destination, item attributes, actual weight, dimensions and reinforcement choice are fixed. The live workflow returns three hypothetical candidates; no prices, route names or delivery promises below represent PikoBuy data.

Candidate A: cheap but not yet eligible

A shows the lowest amount, but its rules are unclear for the rigid accessory. Mark it “needs confirmation.” Do not rank it first until the item attribute is accepted in writing or the live route becomes clearly eligible.

Candidate B: eligible with dimension-sensitive billing

B accepts the contents and shows a clear billable-weight result. Its current cost is higher because the reinforced carton occupies more volume. Keep it on the shortlist and link the quote to the final outer measurements.

Candidate C: eligible with stronger tracking evidence

C costs more than B and shows a different stated service range, but its current terms provide clearer event visibility for this destination. That matters because the parcel has a fixed use date. It does not prove faster delivery; it makes the trade-off easier to document.

  1. Reject no candidate solely because of price.
  2. Confirm A's content eligibility or remove it.
  3. Verify that B and C use the same parcel revision.
  4. Save current amounts, billable results and quote times.
  5. Compare tracking and claim evidence without inventing success rates.
  6. Select the route that meets the deadline tolerance and risk boundary.
  7. Archive the losing quotes so the decision remains auditable.

Repeat the critical checks immediately before payment

Reopen the parcel and confirm destination, item list, attributes, packaging, actual weight and dimensions. Make sure the selected route is still eligible and that its current amount and billing result match the saved row. Review visible service, restriction, insurance and claim terms again.

Save the final route label, quote time, payable amount, transaction reference and the exact parcel revision. If any input has changed, generate a new comparison rather than editing the old values in place. After dispatch, keep tracking events and carrier handoffs in a separate timeline.

The strongest PikoBuy shipping line comparison is deliberately temporary. It records why one live option suited one parcel at one time, while leaving room for the next parcel to produce a different answer.
intro: There is no permanent “best” route for every parcel. Freeze the destination and packed parcel, remove ineligible choices, then compare the current evidence that will actually affect cost, tracking and risk.

title: PikoBuy Shipping Cost: Build a Total Landed Cost Worksheet
description: Build a PikoBuy total landed-cost worksheet for product price, domestic delivery, warehouse decisions, packing, international shipping and destination charges.
body:
PikoBuy total landed cost is bigger than the product price

Total landed cost is the amount required to move a chosen product through purchase, domestic delivery, warehouse decisions, parcel preparation, international transportation and any destination-side amount that applies. It is not one permanent PikoBuy fee. Different actors create different lines, and several amounts do not exist until later in the process.

PikoBuy’s current beginner guide separates the order into stages. A shopper chooses specifications, colour and size, pays for the purchasing order, waits for warehouse receipt and inspection, then selects a shipping route and pays international shipping. The official estimator asks for destination, product type, weight and dimensions. Those facts explain why a product-page price cannot predict the delivered total.

Use a worksheet to prevent category errors. Seller-to-warehouse delivery is not international freight. A return deduction is not part of a normal completed purchase. A route estimate is not the final charge. Destination taxes are not a fixed platform add-on. When each line has a stage and confidence label, comparison becomes much more honest.

Separate the budget into six cost stages

StagePossible linesWhen to verify
ProductSelected variant, quantity and seller priceBefore paying the purchasing order
DomesticSeller delivery to the warehouseOn the source listing and order record
WarehouseOnly confirmed optional photos, handling or return costsWhen the item arrives and the option is shown
PackingOnly current selected packing servicesDuring parcel preparation
InternationalRoute charge based on final parcel inputsAt parcel submission
DestinationTaxes, duties or carrier charges if applicableUsing current destination rules and shipment facts

Do not fill empty cells with numbers copied from another order. A different product type, box shape, destination or route can change the result. Keep a blank or “unknown” value until you have evidence. That is more useful than a precise-looking guess.

Also keep currency separate. Record the original amount and currency, the conversion used for your planning view and the date. Do not mix amounts converted on different dates without saying so. This article does not claim a permanent exchange-rate markup or payment fee because the current checkout is the correct place to verify any such amount.

Build a PikoBuy cost worksheet with status and evidence

Create one row for every real charge and five columns: stage, original amount, planning currency, status, and evidence. Status should be one of known , live estimate , scenario allowance , or unknown . Evidence might be a current listing option, order record, warehouse selection or live route screen. Keep private account and address details out of any shared worksheet.

Planning total = known costs + current route estimate + clearly labelled allowances

The formula is intentionally not “final landed cost.” Before the parcel is measured and the route is chosen, you have a planning total. When final packing measurements and current route charges exist, replace the estimate. When destination treatment is confirmed, update the destination row. Keep the earlier value in a note so you can see what changed.

Add a per-item allocation only after the parcel total is understood. If several products share one parcel, allocate international cost using a method that matches the question. Weight share is simple for similarly shaped goods. A bulky item may need a larger share when it drives box dimensions. Do not divide freight equally merely because there are four items.

Use the PikoBuy shipping estimator as a scenario tool

PikoBuy’s public shipping estimator requests a destination and estimated weight and dimensions, then compares available routes. That makes it useful before warehouse arrival, but only when the inputs are realistic. A clothing-only scenario should not be reused for shoes with retail boxes, a fragile object or a route-sensitive product.

Run at least two scenarios: a conservative packed estimate and an optimized-but-plausible estimate. Record the date, destination, product category, weight, length, width and height used. If the available route list changes when one item is included, note the restriction effect separately instead of treating it as a normal price difference.

After packing, replace assumptions with actual parcel measurements shown for the shipment. A final price can differ because estimated product weight, outer dimensions, packaging choices or route availability changed. The worksheet should explain the difference rather than hiding it.

Worked example: compare a hoodie and boxed shoes without fake rates

Assume a shopper is considering one hoodie and one pair of shoes. The source pages show the selected product prices and any seller-to-warehouse delivery. Those are known order-stage lines. The goods have not arrived, so warehouse weights and final parcel dimensions are unknown. Do not invent them.

  1. Record each selected variant and its current seller price.
  2. Record domestic delivery separately for each seller.
  3. Create Scenario A with both items and the shoe box retained.
  4. Create Scenario B with only confirmed removable packaging changed after warehouse review.
  5. Enter each scenario’s destination, weight and dimensions into the live estimator.
  6. Label the route results “live estimate,” not “paid.”
  7. After receipt, inspect both products before deciding whether either belongs in a parcel.
  8. Replace scenario inputs with the final packed parcel measurements and current route selection.

Suppose Scenario A is above budget. That does not prove the shoes are a bad purchase. Test which variable drives the result: product weight, shoe-box volume, packing choice or route restriction. The next decision may be removing packaging, splitting the parcel, returning an eligible item within the applicable window, or postponing shipment. The worksheet identifies the driver; it does not make the choice for you.

Use budget gates before paying each stage

Set three limits: order-stage limit, parcel-stage limit and delivered planning limit. The order-stage limit prevents a low source price from justifying uncontrolled add-ons. The parcel-stage limit decides whether the final weight, dimensions and available route still make sense. The delivered planning limit includes any reasonable destination allowance without pretending that legal treatment is guaranteed.

At order payment, ask whether the chosen variant and domestic cost fit the first gate. At warehouse approval, ask whether the received product is worth shipping and whether a return decision has a deadline. PikoBuy’s current returns page describes a five-day, 120-hour request window for eligible warehoused items, subject to seller rules, condition, exclusions and costs. Verify eligibility on the live order rather than treating that window as universal free returns.

At parcel payment, use the final route and measurements. Do not compare an old screenshot with a current checkout as if both are equal offers. If the total breaks the limit, change one controllable variable and recalculate. Avoid changing several things at once because you will not know what solved the problem.

Keep uncertain costs visible instead of hiding them

Some destination charges depend on country rules, declared value, product type and carrier process. This guide cannot provide a universal tax or customs number. Use current official destination information for your shipment and label any planning allowance as an allowance. Do not describe it as tax advice or a guarantee of clearance.

International logistics also carries risks that a worksheet cannot price perfectly. PikoBuy’s shipping terms say parcels use third-party logistics providers and identify customs action, damage, loss and peak-season delay among cross-border risks. If a live route offers insurance or another protection option, read the current scope, exclusions and claim process before recording the amount or assuming coverage.

A good worksheet ends with an uncertainty note: which amounts can still change, what event will confirm them, and what maximum the plan can tolerate. That note is often more valuable than another decimal place.
intro: A cheap product can become an expensive delivery, while a higher-priced product can remain reasonable when it packs efficiently. The only useful comparison puts every cost stage into one worksheet and labels what is known, estimated or still uncertain.

title: PikoBuy Tracking Not Updating? Status & Next Steps
description: Check PikoBuy order and parcel tracking: identify the last confirmed stage, understand the three-day tracking checkpoint and prepare a focused support request.
body:
Choose the next step from the last confirmed status

  • Not yet shipped: check purchasing, warehouse approval and parcel payment in the account.
  • Shipped, no tracking information after three days: contact official support with the parcel number, route and shipped timestamp.
  • A tracking number exists but scans have stopped: compare the last carrier event with the selected route information.
  • An address or delivery alert appears: follow the carrier’s specific instructions promptly.

Start by separating four different PikoBuy tracking questions

PikoBuy’s official beginner workflow has six steps: select an item, search or submit its link, place and pay for the purchasing order, wait for warehouse inspection, choose and pay for international shipping, then wait for the parcel. That sequence creates several records. A product order is not an international parcel, a seller’s domestic shipment is not the final carrier route, and a warehouse photo is not proof that the parcel has been dispatched.

StageWhat you are waiting forBest evidence
PurchaseThe requested item is actually bought or refunded if unavailableOrder number, selected option, payment and current order status
Seller to warehouseThe seller sends the item within ChinaSeller or domestic record shown for the order
WarehouseCheck-in, photos and a keep-or-return decisionWarehouse timestamp, photos and item record
International parcelDispatch and third-party carrier trackingParcel number, route, shipped timestamp and tracking number

The exact dashboard wording may change, so do not build a troubleshooting plan around an invented permanent list of status labels. Identify the underlying stage, the actor responsible for the next action and the timestamp that started the wait.

A paid purchasing order is not yet a trackable international shipment

PikoBuy says the first payment follows selection of color, size and quantity. Its guide also says the final price depends on the actual purchase and that an out-of-stock item will be refunded. Until the purchasing result is confirmed, there may be no physical movement to track. Keep the original marketplace link, seller information, option specification and order number together.

If this stage appears unchanged, first check whether the selected option, price or stock requires a response. Do not search an international carrier using a product-order number. Ask a focused question only after recording the order time and current status: “Has this item been purchased from the seller?” is clearer than “Where is my package?”

For a forwarded item rather than an agent-purchased order, PikoBuy’s Shipping Terms describe a different path: obtain the warehouse address, provide it to the sender, submit the forwarding form and wait for warehouse receipt. Missing goods at receipt should be checked with the sender, and the policy says PikoBuy does not compensate for shortages it did not cause.

Warehouse status answers an inspection question, not a delivery question

After receipt, PikoBuy says it checks the item in, takes photos and looks for defects. Review identity, selected option, quantity and visible condition before adding the item to a parcel. If a crucial label or measurement is missing, the Shipping Terms say additional detailed photos can be purchased; the public page does not publish a permanent number or price.

Record when the item became warehoused because other decisions can depend on it. PikoBuy’s current returns page uses a five-day, 120-hour request window for eligible items beginning from the next hour after the status becomes “Warehoused.” That is not an international tracking clock. It is a warehouse decision deadline that depends on eligibility, condition and seller rules.

An item can remain at the warehouse because the shopper has not approved it or built a parcel. It cannot receive international carrier scans until a parcel is selected, a route is chosen, international shipping is paid and dispatch occurs. Keep product-order and parcel records separate to avoid reporting the wrong identifier.

Use the shipped timestamp as the start of PikoBuy parcel tracking

PikoBuy’s beginner guide says tracking information will be available within three days after the parcel is shipped. This is the clearest published checkpoint for initial tracking information; it is not a promise that delivery will finish in three days. Record the exact shipped timestamp, selected route, parcel number and any carrier tracking number displayed.

During the first three days, distinguish “no tracking number” from “a number exists but has no carrier event.” Those are different questions. The first concerns data assignment or handoff; the second may concern carrier acceptance or the first scan. Do not invent a carrier explanation from silence alone.

Once tracking appears, save the latest event text, location and time exactly as displayed. A status summary inside an agent account and the underlying carrier page may update at different moments. Compare timestamps rather than assuming one view is wrong because its wording differs.

When PikoBuy parcel tracking is not updating, diagnose the last confirmed handoff

Start with the last event you can prove. If the account does not show “shipped,” the parcel may still be in warehouse processing or dispatch preparation. If it is shipped but no tracking information appears after the published three-day checkpoint, contact official support with the parcel record. If a carrier scan exists and then stops, the next useful question concerns the third-party route and that last scan.

PikoBuy’s policies state that international parcels are carried by third-party logistics providers. They also identify customs action, damage, loss and peak-season delay as cross-border risks that cannot be eliminated. Those are possible risk categories, not a diagnosis for a particular quiet tracking page. Do not claim customs detention, loss or a missed flight without an event or support confirmation.

Use one sensible waiting rule: compare the quiet period with the current route information shown when you paid, then look for a carrier event or official message. The public pages do not provide one universal delivery time for every destination and route, so this guide does not invent a fixed “late after X days” threshold.

Prepare a compact evidence packet before contacting support

  1. State whether the issue concerns a product order, warehouse item or international parcel.
  2. Include the relevant order or parcel number, but remove it from any public post.
  3. Record the selected route and shipped timestamp exactly as displayed.
  4. Copy the tracking number, last event, location and event time.
  5. Note the destination country and whether the address changed after submission.
  6. Describe the desired answer: purchase confirmation, warehouse receipt, tracking assignment or carrier update.
  7. Keep screenshots private if they show a name, address, telephone number, payment or tracking identifier.

A focused request might say: “Parcel status shows shipped at the recorded time, but no tracking information has appeared after three days. Please confirm whether a carrier number has been assigned.” It avoids accusing a carrier of loss before the evidence supports that conclusion.

Treat address, failed delivery and claims as separate problems

PikoBuy’s Terms of Service say that if a parcel already sent overseas is returned because no one received it, the address was incorrect or incomplete, or delivery failed, the user bears the reshipping cost. Verify recipient name, street, unit, postcode, region and contact number before parcel payment. A tracking alert about an address should be handled as an address problem, not simply a slow shipment.

If the outer package appears damaged at delivery, PikoBuy recommends checking it when signing. Save photographs of visible condition and follow the current carrier or route claim instructions. The Terms say PikoBuy can act as a communication agent with the third-party logistics provider, while compensation follows that provider’s standards.

Insurance also requires precise reading. PikoBuy’s terms describe compensation for an insured lost parcel subject to the insurance conditions and exclusions. Insurance does not turn every delay or customs event into a covered loss. Use the policy attached to the selected route rather than another shopper’s result.

A hypothetical tracking timeline that avoids false conclusions

Imagine an order paid on Monday, confirmed purchased on Tuesday and received at the warehouse on Friday. Photos are approved on Saturday. The shopper creates and pays for an international parcel on Sunday, but the account marks it shipped on Tuesday. The official three-day tracking checkpoint starts from Tuesday’s shipped event—not from the original Monday purchase or Sunday parcel payment.

If no tracking information exists after that checkpoint, the useful evidence is the parcel number, route and Tuesday timestamp. If a number appears on Thursday and the first carrier scan occurs Friday, the initial tracking question is resolved. A later quiet period must be evaluated from Friday’s last confirmed event and the live route information, not from the purchasing date.

This example does not claim that PikoBuy normally purchases, warehouses or ships within those intervals. It shows how one order contains several clocks. Keeping a short timeline prevents an ordinary warehouse wait from being mislabeled as an international delay.
intro: Check whether you are tracking a product order or an international parcel. PikoBuy’s beginner guide says tracking information becomes available within three days after the parcel is shipped—not three days after product payment.

title: Pikobuy W2C Guide 2026: QC Photos, Spreadsheet Research and Shipping Workflow
description: Check PikoBuy W2C sources, warehouse QC photos and shipping decisions with a practical, category-specific 2026 checklist.
body:
Why Use a Pikobuy Spreadsheet?

A spreadsheet helps buyers organize products from different sources. Instead of saving random pages, users can record product names, categories, links, size information, QC notes and shipping considerations. This creates a repeatable research system.

For beginners, this method makes Chinese marketplace shopping easier because every product decision has supporting information. For experienced buyers, spreadsheets become a history record for future purchases.

Understanding W2C Product Routes

W2C means where to find a product. A useful W2C route should include enough context: what the item is, where it comes from, what details need checking and what possible risks exist.

Before moving forward, buyers should compare product information, images and available options. A link alone does not provide enough information for a confident decision.

How QC Photos Improve Decisions

QC photos are one of the most important steps before international shipping. They allow buyers to review visible details including shape, color, stitching, visible material appearance, labels and accessories.

Different products require different checks. Shoes should be reviewed for symmetry and construction. Clothing requires attention to measurements, fabric appearance and tags. Accessories require checking hardware and finishing.

Planning Shipping Before Final Submission

International shipping depends on many factors including destination, parcel weight, package volume and route selection. Good preparation means checking product details first and selecting shipping after QC approval.

A Better Buyer Workflow

A practical workflow is simple: discover products, save W2C information, review QC photos, confirm details, organize the parcel and complete shipping preparation.

The goal of a structured process is reducing mistakes and creating a smoother shopping experience.

Advanced Spreadsheet Tips

Experienced buyers can add extra notes such as previous purchase experience, sizing feedback, shipping performance and product comparisons. Over time, the spreadsheet becomes a personal shopping database.

Conclusion

Pikobuy research works best when buyers combine product discovery, W2C understanding, QC review and shipping planning. A clear workflow helps transform scattered information into organized purchasing decisions.

Use a handoff checklist at each stage

At discovery, retain the source, seller and exact option. At purchasing, confirm the selected variant and paid amount. At warehouse receipt, compare the actual item with that saved specification. At parcel submission, check the contents and live route eligibility. At delivery, inspect the package before disposing of evidence.

An unresolved question should remain visible until the responsible stage can answer it. A seller can clarify a chart, the warehouse can photograph a label, and a carrier can report a delivery event. Asking the right party about a documented detail is more effective than using one broad complaint for every stage.
intro: Buying products from China requires more than finding a link. A reliable workflow combines product discovery, W2C research, QC photo review and shipping preparation.

title: PikoBuy Parcel Spreadsheet: Record Weight, QC & Final Cost
description: Build a parcel-level PikoBuy spreadsheet with item decisions, measured weight, packing, route quotes and delivery records.
body:
Use two linked records

Give each researched item a short reference of your own. Record its source URL, seller, selected size or model, quantity, product cost and domestic delivery. Keep private account identifiers in a private sheet. Use the same reference in a separate parcel table after you decide to ship it.

A parcel can contain several orders, and one order may be split between parcels. Repeating the full parcel freight in every item row would overstate your total. Record the parcel cost once, then document any allocation method used to compare individual items.

Record the warehouse decision

For each item, record arrival, the photos reviewed, missing evidence and the final keep-or-return decision. Use a specific status such as awaiting measurement, acceptable to ship or return requested. Avoid a single vague checked label that conceals an unresolved size or variant question.

Keep the seller’s promised specification beside your observations. A photograph can show a mismatched color or label; it cannot prove composition or long-term function. If a return might be needed, inspect the current eligibility and deadline as soon as the item is received.

Separate estimates from measured values

Before the warehouse receives an item, mark its weight and dimensions as estimates. After measurement, enter the available actual figures and the measurement date. Preserve the estimate in a separate column if you want to learn how accurate your earlier budgets were.

At parcel level, record packed length, width, height and scale weight. Packing can change both weight and volume. Use the chosen route’s actual billing rule rather than a universal volumetric divisor. An item’s loose dimensions cannot be assumed to equal its contribution to the finished box.

Compare route quotes on the same parcel

Record the destination, contents, date, dimensions and weight used for each quote. Compare eligible routes using the same assumptions. Include the displayed tracking, estimated transit window, optional services and any insurance terms that affect your choice.

Keep product costs, domestic delivery, warehouse services, international freight and potential destination costs separate. A coupon should reduce only the charge to which it applies. Record its eligibility, expiry and actual checkout reduction rather than treating an advertised percentage as a discount on the entire order.

Close the record after delivery

Add the dispatched date, selected route, last tracking event and delivery result. Keep any cost adjustment or claim outcome as its own entry. This lets you distinguish a high initial estimate from a genuinely high final expense.

If you allocate a parcel’s freight among items, state the method. Equal shares may be simple but misleading when one item is bulky; weight-based allocation may also miss volumetric effects. Use the allocation for your own comparison, not as a claim that the carrier billed each item separately.

A practical final review

Before parcel payment, filter for unresolved QC questions, missing dimensions and items that are not approved to keep. Confirm the exact contents, recipient details, eligible route and final quote. Preserve the quote and packing evidence with the parcel row.

After receipt, compare the delivered contents with the saved list. Use the completed record to improve the next purchase: which measurements were useful, which packaging was unnecessary and which estimates were too optimistic. The spreadsheet should support decisions, not merely accumulate links.
